# #3543: Patch: Stinkyscape+ E3, Flexible, Evasive and Frenzy
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

Part of fullsend 1 of the Stinkyscape+ set (#3534, tracker #3533). It builds **Flexible**, **Evasive** and **Frenzy**, and migrates the shipped cards: every Unit that can't be attacked gains Evasive, every "after this kills a Unit it may attack again" gains Frenzy, and every Flying Unit has Flexible innately.

The plan: [`docs/stinkyscape-plus-set.md`](https://github.com/jlore-studios/jackioh/blob/claude/laughing-wright-eaibe9/docs/stinkyscape-plus-set.md) (SP2, SP3, SP4, SP8, SP10); the designer's list: [`JackiOh_StinkyscapePlus_Cards.md`](https://github.com/jlore-studios/jackioh/blob/claude/laughing-wright-eaibe9/JackiOh_StinkyscapePlus_Cards.md). Both are on the planning branch `claude/laughing-wright-eaibe9` until the foundation (#3535) brings them onto this fullsend's branch. Where they disagree with SPEC, SPEC wins (CLAUDE.md). `{For AI: …}` notes in the designer's text are the designer's notes to you, the builder, not to the game's AI (SP5).

## The designer's words

```text
* **Flexible (New Keyword)**
  * Can be played in the unit row or the back row
* **Frenzy (New Keyword)**
  * **Frenzy** [effect]
  * **Frenzy** triggers the effect after the unit attacks and destroys a unit
  * So for example **Frenzy** can attack again would equate to **After this kills a unit it may attack again**
  * Give frenzy to all past cards with this effect
  * Nerfs can get rid of **Frenzy** keyword
  * Unit being buffed or gaining a random key word can gain the combat keyword **Frenzy** with “**Frenzy** this may attack again” and this
* **Evasive (New Keyword)**
  * Same thing as **Can’t be attacked**
  * Give all units with **Can’t be attacked** this
  * Units with **Evasive** implicitly have **Can’t Defend** (similar to indestructible)
  * A nerf can remove **Evasive**
```

The owner, 2026-11-09, on Flexible: "units in the backrow CAN attack & act as a normal unit. Think of it as flying units <-- innately have flexible".

## The build (change a default only with a ruling note)

- **Flexible** (the owner's call): "Can be played in the unit row or the back row." The player picks the row as they play it. A Unit in the backrow **can attack and acts as a normal Unit**, as a Flying Unit in the backrow already does: §6.1 Flying lets a Flying Unit be played into an empty backrow zone, where it is a Unit for every rule (R1081000; summons and "fill your board", R2248000). **Flying Units innately have Flexible.** Flexible is that placement made a keyword any card may have, and Flying grants it instead of carrying the rule itself. Flying Units behave exactly as before, so no shipped Flying card plays differently, and a test proves it. **Default:** a Flexible Field Spell may be played into a unit zone and keeps working there as a Field Spell; one with printed stats (#59 Mass Driver) is also a Unit there, which can be attacked and can attack. Write the ruling.
- **Evasive**: "Same thing as Can't be attacked … Units with Evasive implicitly have Can't Defend … A nerf can remove Evasive." It is a keyword. Every shipped card that says "Can't be attacked" gets Evasive instead (a catalog migration, since those cards gain Can't Defend). **Default:** a card that has both shows Evasive alone.
- **Frenzy [effect]**: "triggers the effect after the unit attacks and destroys a unit." "Frenzy: this may attack again" means "After this kills a unit it may attack again". Every shipped card with that effect gains the keyword. A Nerf can remove Frenzy, and the random-keyword pools (a Buff's, "gain a random keyword") gain "Frenzy: this may attack again" as a combat keyword.

## The cards that will use it

S07 and S08 (the Mindustrial turrets), S09 (#50 Graphite's Frenzy), S10 and S11 (Flexible field spells and #58 Phase Conveyer), every Flying Unit, and every shipped card the migration touches.

## The shipped cards

The migration changes how shipped cards play (Evasive brings Can't Defend, and the random-keyword pools change), so the release's pending fragment must claim them. Record the cards in `spec/pending/<this issue>.md` and in a table in the part's final comment: each card's id, name, old keywords and new ones. A card in BUILD's must-pass tables (M13 and before) gets its row updated.

- [ ] The mechanic is written into the spec's sections it changes (§3, §4, §6 Flying and the new rows, §10), with ruling notes numbered in this issue's block, tests named after them, and the paragraph in `spec/pending/<this issue>.md` (CLAUDE.md rule 3).
- [ ] It is proved on fixture scripts in `crates/engine/tests/rules*` (the `testkit` feature's `scenario()`): a Flexible Unit played into the backrow attacks, is attacked and defends as a normal Unit, and a Flying Unit's placement is unchanged. The migrated shipped cards' own tests are updated in their script files.
- [ ] The view (`view_for`) and the wire carry what it shows (`docs/v0.3.0/SURFACE.md` for any boundary it adds; `cargo test … --features jackioh-engine/ts` rewrites `apps/web/src/wire/`), and the client offers both rows when a Flexible card is played, as it already does for Flying.
